status: Source-only design and bounded original-operation proof. Root authorized finite C implementation and controls after this proof; no C mutation/build/runtime yet.
requested_consumer: Actual Node v24.13 FSReqPromise live request.Get('promise') selection and Promise::Resolver::Resolve/Reject on that same genuine Promise.
proposed_abi: JSValue JS_PiSettlePromise(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst promise, JSValueConst value, bool is_reject);
contract: Both inputs remain borrowed; a genuine Promise is required. Result is owned undefined or exception sentinel under the normal caller-owned guest boundary.
Existing actual pending exception short-circuits before any property access or mutation; caller must retain both values through the operation.
Intrinsic class/opaque validation rejects non-Promise values without public Promise, prototype or constructor lookup.

A Promise already fulfilled or rejected returns success before observing the resolution value; pending adoption remains pending and permits a later direct native Resolve/Reject call, as V8 Resolver does.

Extract the existing QuickJS resolving-function value tail into one internal helper. Keep original function-specific already_resolved handling before that helper, unchanged. The new bridge calls the same helper after its direct Promise guard.
Do not allocate new resolving function wrappers, construct a new output Promise, change reaction scheduling, change existing fatal selection, or conflate fulfillment with thenable resolution.
Pending after the borrowed operation must be reported through the exception sentinel while leaving the actual reason intact.
evidence_conclusions: V8 Resolver::GetPromise returns the same JSPromise object.
V8 Resolver Resolve/Reject checks only current Promise::kPending before calling the internal operation; it has no cross-call resolving-function latch.

V8 internal Resolve rejects self-resolution, fulfills primitives, gets live then, converts ordinary getter failure into rejection, escapes uncatchable failure, and enqueues a real thenable job for callable then.
QuickJS fulfill_or_reject_promise alone omits required thenable adoption.
The existing public JS_GetTypedArrayType(value)>=0 || JS_IsDataView(value) exactly implements nonthrowing ArrayBufferView brand detection; no companion C bridge is needed.
proposed_controls: Fresh intrinsic Promise scalar fulfillment and rejection preserve the selected Promise identity and raw value identity.
An actually settled Promise skips later live then lookup on repeated direct Resolve and Reject.
Live then getter executes synchronously once; selected then executes only at real job checkpoint; raw this and argument shapes are preserved.
Direct repeated calls while a thenable is pending remain admitted; a later native Reject/primitive Resolve may settle before the older queued thenable.
Original ordinary resolving function pair retains its one-shot latch after the internal helper extraction.
Self-resolution and an ordinary throwing then getter reject the same selected Promise with real reasons.
Noncallable then fulfills with the original object; a returned flagged Error value remains DATA.
Fresh real foreign-realm Promise works, while proxies/non-Promises are rejected without a guest constructor or prototype lookup.
Prior actual pending exception preserves reason and prevents any then getter or Promise state mutation.
Actual fatal from a live then getter escapes before job enqueue, preserving producer identity and own-data no-later-progress.
Actual selected then/value/job owners remain alive while queued, and retire once after completion; borrowed input roots remain caller-owned.
Live request Set/Get fixture selects a different genuine Promise, then intrinsic settlement affects exactly that selected object.
remaining_limits: C implementation and control source remain to be authored within Root's finite authorized scope.
V8 external Promise hook/debugger and full cross-engine allocation-layout parity are not newly claimed.
No AsyncWrap prototype or native immediate owner is supplied by this bridge.
No execution or public fs/promises qualification.
